lines.text: But to You, O LORD, I cry for help;
in the morning my prayer comes before You.
Why, O LORD, do You reject me?
Why do You hide Your face from me?
From my youth I was afflicted and near death.
I have borne Your terrors; I am in despair.
Your wrath has swept over me;
All day long they engulf me like water;
they enclose me on every side.
You have removed my beloved and my friend;

pictures.scene: Peder Balke, Træ i vinterskov — the bare tree alone in the white emptiness, or Your righteousness in the land of oblivion, but to You O LORD I cry for help
pictures.name: pd_balke_vinterskov

pictures.scene: Vilhelm Hammershøi, Interior with a woman seen from behind — the woman standing in the quiet morning room with her face turned away, in the morning my prayer comes before You, why O LORD do You reject me
pictures.name: pd_hammershoi_interieur

pictures.scene: Christian Krohg, Sick Girl — the girl propped up in the chair with a rose going to pieces in her lap, why do You hide Your face from me, from my youth I was afflicted and near death
pictures.name: pd_krohg_syk_pike

pictures.scene: Jakub Schikaneder, A Street Corner in Prague — the huddled figures crossing the empty street at night, I have borne Your terrors I am in despair, Your wrath has swept over me
pictures.name: pd_schikaneder_praha

pictures.scene: Johan Christian Dahl, Shipwreck on the Coast of Norway — the ship broken on the rocks with the surf running over her, Your terrors have destroyed me, all day long they engulf me like water
pictures.name: pd_dahl_skipsvrak

pictures.scene: Walter Langley, Never Morning Wore to Evening but Some Heart Did Break — the young widow bent double on the harbour wall with the old woman's hand on her shoulder, they enclose me on every side, You have removed my beloved and my friend
pictures.name: pd_langley_never_morning

pictures.scene: Knud Baade, Mondnacht — the lone fisherman beside his boat under a clouded moon, darkness is my closest companion
pictures.name: pd_baade_mondnacht
